facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old African American female
elevated intraocular pressure at age 13
taller stature than her relatives (180.4 cm)
long fingers
hypermobility of the shoulders, digits, and knees
Family history was negative for similar findings
Serial echocardiograms showed no abnormalities
Open iridocorneal angle in each eye
No evidence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
Subtle lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye (first observed at age 17)
Later developed lens dislocation in the left eye (at age 32)
2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene (c.709C>T p.Arg237* and c.3776-1G>C splice acceptor)

aliases: Ectopia lentis with short stature and brachydactyly
concepts.why: The patient's elevated intraocular pressure, lens dislocation, and genetic variants in the LTBP2 gene are consistent with Weill-Marchesani syndrome, a rare genetic disorder characterized by ectopia lentis, short stature, and brachydactyly.

The patient's tall stature, long fingers, and hypermobility of the shoulders, digits, and knees, as well as the lens dislocation, are consistent with Marfan syndrome, a genetic disorder that affects the body's connective tissue.

The patient's hypermobility of the shoulders, digits, and knees, as well as the tall stature and long fingers, are consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, a group of genetic disorders that affect the body's connective tissue.
The patient's lens dislocation is consistent with homocystinuria, a genetic disorder that affects the metabolism of the amino acid homocysteine and can cause ectopia lentis.
